headline.title: Why Do Naive SFT Filters For Safety Properties Fail?
headline.summary: The Google DeepMind Language Model Interpretability team discusses the limitations of naive supervised fine-tuning (SFT) filters in ensuring safety properties in language models. Their research indicates that filtering SFT data often fails to effectively eliminate undesirable outcomes, highlighting the need for improved strategies in model safety.

articles.title: As AI companies race to go public, who else is along for the ride?
articles.summary: As AI companies prepare for public offerings, numerous startups are seeking to capitalize on the momentum generated by high-profile IPOs like SpaceX. This trend highlights the growing interest and investment in the AI sector as firms aim to leverage the current market enthusiasm.

articles.title: China may have accessed Mythos
articles.summary: A report from Semafor indicates that the White House's export restrictions on Anthropic's Mythos were influenced by concerns that it may have been accessed by a group associated with China. If confirmed, such access could pose significant national security risks.

articles.title: Meta reportedly moves to unwind $2B Manus deal after Beijing’s demand
articles.summary: Meta is reportedly beginning to unwind its $2 billion acquisition of Manus following a directive from Beijing to reverse the deal. This move comes amid ongoing scrutiny of foreign investments in China's tech sector.

articles.title: As Anthropic suspends access to new models, India debates its AI future
articles.summary: Anthropic has suspended access to its new AI models, prompting discussions among Indian tech leaders about the implications for the country's AI development strategy. The incident is seen as a potential wake-up call for India to reassess its approach to artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Amazon security research reportedly led to the White House’s Anthropic Fable ban
articles.summary: Amazon's cybersecurity research and discussions between CEO Andy Jassy and the White House reportedly influenced the export control directive that resulted in Anthropic's decision to restrict access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. The Wall Street Journal highlights that the findings from Amazon's research played a key role in this regulatory action.

articles.title: Anthropic cuts off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access following government order
articles.summary: Anthropic has ceased access to its AI models Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all users, including its employees, following a government order citing national security concerns. The order mandates that access be blocked for all foreign nations, both inside and outside the United States.

articles.title: SFT Drives Gemini’s Safety Properties
articles.summary: A recent update from the Google DeepMind Language Model Interpretability team reveals that the safety properties of the Gemini model are primarily influenced by the combination of pretraining and supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rather than reinforcement learning. The findings suggest that these safety features may not be universally applicable to other model families.

articles.title: KPMG pulls report on AI usage due to apparent hallucinations
articles.summary: KPMG has retracted a report on AI usage after discovering inaccuracies attributed to AI-generated content, commonly referred to as "hallucinations." The incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding the reliability of AI-generated information in research and reporting.

articles.title: Amazon CEO reportedly raised Anthropic model concerns before government crackdown
articles.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reportedly raised security concerns regarding Anthropic's models, prompting the company to restrict global access to two of its AI models. This action comes ahead of potential government regulations on AI technologies.

articles.title: My yard is dying, so I made an app for that
articles.summary: A developer created an app using Gemini to address issues in their yard, resulting in a functional prototype alongside a bug notification. The app's interface included a button to resolve the identified bug, showcasing Gemini's capabilities in app development.

articles.title: Apple’s new AI photo editing tools mostly work, for better and worse
articles.summary: Apple has introduced new AI photo editing tools in iOS 27, marking a significant enhancement for its camera capabilities. While these features show promise, they are considered less advanced compared to those available on competitors like Google's Pixel phones.
